pages.title: How to Fly
pages.text: Do not believe anyone who makes flight control sound impossibly advanced. The controls are actually quite simple.$(br2)Tip: every control can be rebound in the key settings.$(br2)When you first right-click to sit in the Control Seat, view lock is disabled, so you can look around freely. Use W/S to pitch, A/D to roll, Tab to increase throttle, and Ctrl to decrease it. Positive throttle moves forward; negative throttle moves backward.

Press Left Alt to toggle view lock. When enabled, your view aligns with the Control Seat and ordinary mouse-look is disabled. Moving the mouse vertically controls pitch and moving it horizontally controls yaw. A/D still controls roll, while W/S now translates the vessel upward or downward. Tab and Ctrl continue to control throttle.$(br2)To leave the Control Seat, disable view lock first, then press Shift.

pages.title: Other Controls
pages.text: You may notice that the Control Seat automatically applies opposing force and torque as damping. This keeps an accidental input from spinning you into a cyclone or launching you into the sky before burying you underground. Experienced pilots—or anyone who simply dislikes assistance—can toggle linear and angular damping with B and H respectively.$(br2)AeroIE accepts no responsibility for lost subspaces, memory explosions, corrupted worlds, or motion sickness caused by disabling these aids.

Press G to toggle antigravity. It lets you remain airborne without flying at high speed or attaching a huge balloon. Small inaccuracies in Aeronautics physics may cause a slight upward drift, so disable antigravity before leaving a vessel unattended.$(br2)Press L to toggle auto-level. While active, it disables pitch and roll input and applies torque to keep the subspace upright and level. Players familiar with the Eureka Airships helm should recognize the behavior.$(br2)Press V to toggle shields, P to open warp controls, and 1/2/3/4 to toggle the corresponding weapon channels. These systems are explained in their respective chapters.
